newsitem.title: UK: U.S. shares in Britain weak, Dow seen lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shares in Britain weak, Dow seen lower.

text.p: British and European investors were selling U.S. shares in London on Friday as they feared Wall Street could be on the verge of a meltdown after it took a nosedive on Thursday.
"U.S. shares are down across the board. We haven't seen any panic selling, just a general mark down," a share dealer at a U.S. stockbrokers in London said.
"It looks as though the Dow (industrials average of 30 leading U.S. shares) will open about 40 points lower today."
On Thursday, the Dow plunged nearly 100 points and has lost 170 points over the past two days.
Many investors believe that the U.S. share market, which has soared by 30 percent this year, is overpriced and due for a downward correction.
By contrast, London's Financial Times Index of 100 leading British shares has only risen around nine percent in 1996.

The Dow has fallen around 250 points since reaching an all-time record peak of 6,547.79 on November 25 but some stockmarket analysts believe it could lose another 300 points before buyers are tempted to return.
"Even if the Dow falls another 300 points, we're still looking at an annual gain of 20 percent which is a good performance by anyone's standards," one share dealer at a British stockbrokers said.

U.S. automotive shares skidded lower after the international car giant Ford warned that sluggish sales would cause its North American production would to decline by around two percent in the first three months of next year.
Ford was down $1/2 at $31-5/8, Chryler fell $3/8 to $33-1/8, and General Motors, which makes Vauxhall cars in Britain, lost $1/4 at $56-5/8.
